paragraphs: Friend, this is the heaviest passage we've baked, so I'll go slow. Look at what Jesus does the whole way through: He carries His own cross, He is crucified in the middle of two others, and He is never pulled off course (John 19:17-18). The soldiers casting lots for His clothing and Jesus saying "I am thirsty" both happen to fulfill the Scripture (John 19:24, 28). I think the lesson is this: nothing here catches God off guard, and nothing here happens to Jesus without Him knowing.

Now stay with me on one moment, because it's the one that matters. Even from the cross, Jesus sees His mother and the disciple whom He loved, and He puts them in each other's care (John 19:26-27). Then, "knowing that everything had now been accomplished," He says, "It is finished." (John 19:28, 30) Friend, He wasn't saying He ran out of strength. He was saying the work He came to do was complete, and Mark 10:45 says He came to give His life as a ransom for many.

So here's what I want you to carry out of my bakery today. You can't add to what Jesus finished, and you don't have to try. That's good news for every baker who has ever felt forgotten, because He sees you, and He has already done the work for you. And this story is not over, so keep your oven warm.
